newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Maverick Bre-X boss hits Busang jackpot.
newsitem.headline: Maverick Bre-X boss hits Busang jackpot.

text.p: Maverick Canadian miner David Walsh may get his much-desired vacation by the beach after all, having clinched the Busang gold deal after some tense moments for his company, Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
"I figured that when we started this...some major company would buy us out... (I) will go for a vacation on the beach," he told Reuters in an interview in Jakarta recently.

Dressed casually in a beige short-sleeved shirt, matching pants and casual leather shoes, Walsh, 51, recounted how he had taken a gamble with Bre-X's last C$10,000 ($7,400) to visit Indonesia in April 1993 to take an option on the Busang property.
"At that time Bre-X was down to its last C$10,000, which I spent on coming over here," he said. "Our other explorations have been zero. I had never imagined it would be this big."
Bre-X said on Monday it had signed a joint venture agreement with its Indonesian partners and Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States to develop Busang.

It said the company would be 45-percent owned by Bre-X, 30 percent by two Indonesian companies and their partners, 10 percent by the Indonesian government and 15 percent by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States.
"This is a great day for both Bre-X shareholders and for the people of Indonesia," Walsh said in a statement, released in Jakarta, announcing the deal.
There were moments far less joyous for Bre-X and Walsh in their run-up to clinching the Busang deal.

Late last year, the Indonesian government ordered Bre-X to partner Canada's Barrick Gold Corp to develop the property, set beneath tropical rainforests on rolling hills in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province on Borneo island.
Bre-X, which discovered the deposit, estimates the property to contain 70.95 million ounces worth over $24 billion.
Barrick, which was to get a lion's share of the Busang find under the government edict, announced on Monday it was not able to reach an agreement with Bre-X.
Walsh is believed to have swung the deal in favour of Bre-X by teaming up with influential Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, a regular golfing partner of President Suharto.
Hasan, through the Nusamba group which is 80-percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto, has taken controlling stakes in two local firms that have minority shares in Busang.
Walsh conceded in the interview that it had been extremely hard work for him during the past four years.
"Whatever personal success that has come out of this, I haven't had a chance to enjoy it. It's been extremely hard work the last four years," he said.
The Busang deal would certainly make Walsh a wealthy man, but he denied his stake in Bre-X was worth $1.5 billion.
"It's definitely not $1.5 billion. I had probably a 35 or 40 percent stake in Bre-X. When people ask me how much I now have in Bre-X, I say not enough," he said with a laugh.
Walsh said he took the Busang gamble even when others had given up, buying a stake in the property for a mere $80,000.

"Nineteen previous holes were drilled in the central zone (of Busang) that were incorrect," he said. "When a company decided to pull out because it was quiet there, we decided to take the contrary view.

"I had no money but a commitment...that I would finance the exploration and acquisition of Busang I (the central zone)," he said. ""Bre-X was a shell of a company then, with virtually no working capital."
